stances.claim: The PH's slight improvement in TI rankings (141st to 134th) is a very small consolation -- Aquino's anti-corruption crusade had not yet gained global traction in 2010.

Without P-Noy's active leadership, Cha-cha will not succeed -- he is the choreographer, music provider, and host; historically, no Charter change has ever been approved without the sitting president's say-so.
Starting Cha-cha now -- even if only to resolve the two procedural hurdles via SC -- would allow substantive amendments to proceed expeditiously later.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban delivers two messages in one column. First, the PH ranked 134th in the TI 2010 Global Corruption Barometer -- slightly better than 139th (2009) and 141st (2008) but still tied with Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Honduras, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Togo, Ukraine, and Zimbabwe at 2.4; Indonesia has meanwhile risen to 110th under Yudhoyono, 'bequeathing to us the embarrassing basket case title.' Aquino's anti-corruption crusade had not yet gained global traction in 2010. Second, on Cha-cha: Enrile, Belmonte, and Drilon (limiting it to economic provisions) want it on the legislative agenda, but Aquino calls it not a priority. The author argues that without P-Noy's active leadership, no Cha-cha dance party will be held -- historically, every Charter change from Quezon/Roxas through Marcos through Cory was driven by the sitting president. Two procedural hurdles will inevitably require SC resolution: (1) whether the two chambers deliberate separately or jointly in a constituent assembly (Mendoza argues for joint session based on clear intent); and (2) whether the three-fourths vote is computed from 310 total members or from each chamber separately. Starting Cha-cha now -- even just to get these questions resolved -- would allow substantive amendments to proceed expeditiously later.
